title: REST XML not-found, the bare <Error> body with no envelope
why: The other XML shape a body-code carrier arrives in, and the reason the carrier row names two positions rather than one. REST XML's S3 dialect states the code in a root <Error> with no ErrorResponse around it, so a parser that drops the root element — the JS SDK's parseXmlBody and this corpus's rust converter both do — reads the code at the top level, while one that keeps the error node under an Error key — botocore's RestXMLParser does — reads it nested. Both are the same wire, and every backend must answer it whichever way its own stack lands. Verified against internal/protocol's WriteXMLError, which is byte for byte this envelope.
